historical_record.description: Built as a two-storey house, one of three in the district drawn on the Coast Survey's map of 1859.
Polk & Gamble remodelled the parlour with Willis Polk's signature natural redwood panelling and slender fluted columns — the one interior that survives essentially intact.
Enlarged with a third floor, new projections and a natural-shingle skin, probably to Willis Polk's design, turning the old house into a First Bay Area Tradition one.
Altered by the builders Ferguson & Son.
Altered by Wurster, Bernardi & Emmons, including a new entry walkway.
Robert Stern reworked the house again as a shingled design in the First Bay Area Tradition, keeping the exterior shingles and the Polk parlour.

building.completed_conflict: Recorded as built c. 1857; the assessor's roll gives 1900.

notable_residents.name: Horatio Putnam Livermore
notable_residents.detail: The industrialist Horatio Putnam Livermore (1837–1916), builder of the Folsom Dam and power station, bought the house in 1889 and lived here from late 1897 until his death; from it he commissioned so much of the hilltop that his obituary called him the "Father of Russian Hill".

notable_residents.name: Willis Polk
notable_residents.detail: The architect Willis Polk lived here as a tenant before his own house at 1013 Vallejo Street was finished in 1892, and held his "rose leaf parties" here.

notable_residents.name: Norman Banks Livermore
notable_residents.detail: Norman Banks Livermore (1872–1953) — engineer, industrialist, forty-year board member of PG&E — moved in on his father's death and lived here until he moved his family to Marin County about 1930.
